clips.title: The story
paras: The Lich's Identity is an Undercity quest given by Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter. Seeking to uncover the identity of a reclusive lich living on Brightwater Lake, Bethor sends an emissary to steal the figure's spellbook to gauge his power and allegiance.

North of the Undercity, in the misty waters of Brightwater Lake, a lone lich dwells in self-imposed exile on a small island. Unlike the mindless pawns of the Lich King, this necromancer possesses his own free will, yet he lives in deep paranoia. Convinced that any undead who approach him are Scourge thralls sent to drag him back into servitude, he unleashes his summoned minions on anyone setting foot on his shores.

Word of the rogue lich eventually reached Bethor Iceshard, the archmage overseeing the mages in the Undercity. Bethor recognized the strategic importance of such an entity: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner seeks every scrap of magical mastery and every capable will to bolster the Forsaken against their many foes. To assess whether the hermit could be recruited, Bethor requires proof of his identity and necromantic expertise.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: There is a lich who dwells on the island in Brightwater Lake to the north. Although he is a free-willed Forsaken, he believes all other Undead are Scourge slaves and has his minions attack anyone who approaches him.
But because he is Forsaken, the Queen will want him. And if he is skilled in Necromancy, then his knowledge would be...quite useful to us.
To discover his identity and his talents, I must see his spellbook. Steal into his camp and acquire it, then return to me.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Friend, have you acquired the book?

clips.title: Completion
paras: Very good, friend. I will study this book and determine the identity of that lich. You have served your Queen well.
Bethor opens the book and stares intently at its glowing pages...
Astonishing! The book you retrieved belongs to no one other than Gunther Arcanus!
Gunther was a skilled Necromancer in life; he and I were friends and comrades-in-arms, before the Plague. And judging from his book he has grown even more powerful in death.
His skills would be a great boon to us.
